editorial:
Imagine being a kid who is so good with computers that you actually attract the attention of a supernatural entity. That is exactly what happens to Marcin, a young genius who finds himself targeted by the mysterious Computer King. This strange villain lives in a digital underworld where he controls the ghosts of famous scientists and artists from the past. It feels like a weird mix of a kids' adventure and a dark fairy tale. You will feel for Marcin as he realizes that every screen or keyboard he touches could be a trap designed to pull him out of the real world and into a creepy digital kingdom.

The acting is surprisingly solid, and the way they handled the special effects for 1989 gives it a cool, retro vibe. While the story moves a bit slow in the middle, the tension builds up nicely as the Computer King gets closer to winning. If you love old-school tech and stories about gifted kids, you should definitely check this out.
endingExplained: In the final showdown, Marcin has to use his coding skills to outsmart the Computer King. He manages to create a logic loop that traps the villain in his own digital world. By breaking the connection between the real world and the netherworld, Marcin saves himself and frees the trapped souls of the scientists. He wakes up back in his own room, safe and sound, knowing that his brilliance is a gift, not a curse.
targetAudience: Ideal for anyone who loves 80s nostalgia and supernatural stories about tech.
